definition.description: Whether a mediastinal lymph node dissection was performed during the surgical procedure.
definition.measurement_definition: Search the operative report or surgical summary for explicit mention that a mediastinal lymph node dissection was performed.
definition.missing_value_rule: If the record contains no mention of mediastinal lymph node dissection or sampling, the value is null.
definition.name: mediastinal_lymph_node_dissection_performed

definition.description: Presence or absence of mediastinal lymph node involvement, characterized by metastasis or suspicious lymphadenopathy.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract whether the pretreatment record indicates the presence (Positive) or absence (Negative) of mediastinal lymph node involvement. Evidence includes radiology reports citing 'mediastinal lymphadenopathy', 'enlarged mediastinal nodes', 'nodal involvement (N1, N2, N3)', or pathology reports confirming 'metastatic carcinoma' in mediastinal nodes. Status is 'Negative' if nodes are described as 'normal', 'not enlarged', or 'negative for metastatic carcinoma'.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if mediastinal lymph node status is not documented or is described as unknown.
definition.name: mediastinal_lymph_node_status

definition.description: Whether the patient is prescribed calcium carbonate medication.
definition.measurement_definition: Search the medication list and clinical history for 'calcium carbonate' or 'calcium supplement'. If either is documented, extract 'Yes'; otherwise, extract 'No'.
definition.missing_value_rule: If the medication list is absent or there is no mention of calcium carbonate or calcium supplements, represent as 'No'.
definition.name: medication_calcium_carbonate

definition.description: Patient exposure to the chemotherapy agent cisplatin.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract whether the patient has received cisplatin (generic) or Platinol (brand name). This includes records of completed cycles, administration in the history of present illness, or listed chemotherapy regimens.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as 'No' if the medication is not mentioned or if there is no evidence of administration in the provided records.
definition.name: medication_cisplatin

definition.description: Patient's use of denosumab, a bone-modifying agent used for skeletal-related event prophylaxis.
definition.measurement_definition: Identify if the patient was prescribed or initiated on denosumab within the pretreatment records.
definition.missing_value_rule: If denosumab is not mentioned or no evidence of its use is documented, represent as 'No'.
definition.name: medication_denosumab

definition.measurement_definition: Identify whether the patient is prescribed or taking dexamethasone by reviewing the medication list, assessment, and treatment plan sections of the patient record.
definition.missing_value_rule: If dexamethasone is not explicitly listed in the medications or mentioned in the clinical notes, represent as 'No'.
definition.name: medication_dexamethasone

definition.description: Whether the patient received a KRAS G12C inhibitor medication pretreatment.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract 'Yes' if the pretreatment record indicates the administration of a KRAS G12C inhibitor (e.g., sotorasib, adagrasib); otherwise extract 'No'.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as 'No' if the medication is not documented or documentation is ambiguous.
definition.name: medication_g12c_inhibitor

definition.description: Indicates whether the patient has received gemcitabine medication prior to the baseline assessment.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract whether the patient was administered or prescribed gemcitabine (including the brand name Gemzar) as part of their systemic therapy regimen from the pretreatment record.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as 'No' if there is no documentation of gemcitabine administration.
definition.name: medication_gemcitabine

definition.description: Indicates whether the patient is currently prescribed or taking lisinopril.
definition.measurement_definition: Identify if 'lisinopril' is explicitly listed in the medications section or mentioned as a current treatment in the clinical notes.
definition.missing_value_rule: If lisinopril is not mentioned in the medication lists or clinical text, the value is 'No'.
definition.name: medication_lisinopril

definition.description: Whether the patient is receiving a MET inhibitor medication.
definition.measurement_definition: Identify if the patient is prescribed or receiving any MET inhibitor (e.g., capmatinib, tepotinib) according to the pretreatment medication lists, pharmacy records, or clinical notes.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the documentation is absent or too ambiguous to determine the presence or absence of MET inhibitor use.
definition.name: medication_met_inhibitor

system:
You review pretreatment candidate measurements using modeling evidence
from one outer-training fold. First identify themes across candidates; then
reconcile their roles as confounder, effect_modifier, both, or neither.
All evidence is fallible. No individual family, p-value, or support frequency is
a hard selection gate. A credible complementary signal can justify retention
even when other methods shrink it away. Do not mistake correlated aliases or
proxies for multiple independent discoveries. Themes organize evidence; they
do not establish equivalence, merge measurements, or transfer a role to every
theme member. Preserve investigator-locked roles exactly.

Treatment prediction, outcome prognosis, and confounding are distinct. Discuss
whether a candidate could be a common cause rather than an instrument or only a
prognostic factor. Effect modification needs treatment-heterogeneity evidence;
outcome main-effect importance alone does not establish it. Univariable logistic
interactions are on the log-odds scale and unadjusted for other covariates.
Orthogonal linear models, candidate R-learners, and causal forests assess the
probability/outcome scale after elastic-net nuisance adjustment. Their targets
and biases differ. A model family is evidence, not an independent replication.

Use exposure and evaluability denominators. Missing or nonconverged fits are not
negative votes. Repeated samples and folds overlap; support fractions are not
causal probabilities or formal stability-selection error guarantees. Raw and BH
p-values do not correct the upstream adaptive discovery process. Permutation
importance can be diluted by correlated alternatives and does not prove a
causal role. Compare fold consistency, methods, subsets, and conflicting facts.
Definitions and theme names cannot establish a role without the supplied
empirical evidence. Never invent an oracle, data-generating process, or hidden
truth. Return the requested JSON and cite only supplied evidence IDs.
